slides.headline: Starbucks Cards Never Expire. Nonredemption Pays.
slides.subheadline: Follow customer prepayments into interest-free financing—and separate nonredemption revenue from profit.

designSystem.citationTreatment: Render citation markers as compact source references outside headline and numerical spans.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use a 1080×1350 near-black canvas. Place masthead above a thin red rule, followed by the kicker. Stack the monumental headline across four lines; emphasize Nonredemption Pays in red. Add one oversized, unbranded card silhouette with an unbroken white perimeter. Place subheadline beneath it and two compact telemetry badges above the issue footer. No diagrams, arrows, or callout boxes.

slides.headline: Convenience Makes Prepayment Feel Harmless
slides.subheadline: Easy payment and gifting encourage repeat visits; prepaid balances lack bank protections.​

items.title: THE PROMISE
items.body: Convenient payment, gifting and rewards make keeping money inside Starbucks feel useful.

items.title: THE CONTRACT
items.body: Balances prepay merchandise, earn no interest, and carry no FDIC insurance.

slides.svgBlueprint: Divide the content field into two equal vertical panels with a red hairline. On the left, draw a minimal gift-card outline above THE PROMISE; on the right, draw an open contract bracket above THE CONTRACT. Anchor one dated evidence badge inside each panel. Use 48px numerals, generous internal padding, and no bank-vault imagery.

slides.headline: The Big Balances Mix Different Obligations
slides.subheadline: Neither September 28, 2025 balance isolates outstanding gift-card principal.

items.title: CURRENT BALANCE-SHEET LINE
items.body: Combines stored-value liabilities and current deferred revenue, including Nestlé’s $177.0 million prepaid royalty balance.

items.title: CARD-AND-LOYALTY BALANCE
items.body: Includes unredeemed Stars alongside cards—not gift-card principal alone.

slides.svgBlueprint: Stack two offset surface-colored cards, the upper card wider than the lower. Give each a red category tab, a 52px numerical badge, a separate million unit, and its qualification directly underneath. Add overlapping outline layers behind both cards to signal mixed categories, without implying proportional composition. Keep the date in the subheadline.

slides.headline: No Expiration Does Not Mean No Breakage
slides.subheadline: Expected nonuse becomes revenue without a fixed card-confiscation deadline.​

items.title: LOAD
items.body: Customer loads initially create deferred revenue: Starbucks has cash but still owes merchandise.

items.title: REDEEM
items.body: Spending the balance converts deferred revenue into revenue.

items.title: ESTIMATE NONUSE
items.body: Historical patterns and applicable unclaimed-property remittances inform nonredemption estimates, recognized proportionately as cards redeem.

slides.svgBlueprint: Draw a vertical white spine with three surface-filled nodes labeled LOAD, REDEEM, and ESTIMATE NONUSE. Branch a short red line from the redemption node toward the estimate node to show proportional recognition, not a countdown. Align each body beside its node. Place two small telemetry badges in the footer; never depict the one-year observation as an expiration deadline.

slides.kicker: THE RECEIPTS / REVENUE, NOT NET PROFIT
slides.headline: The Receipts Establish Revenue, Not Profit
slides.subheadline: Two disclosed components produce the fiscal 2025 total.

items.title: COMPANY-OPERATED STORES
items.body: Card breakage recognized in company-operated store revenues.

items.title: LICENSED STORES
items.body: Card breakage recognized in licensed store revenues.

items.title: CALCULATED TOTAL
items.body: Breakage revenue—not interest income or proof of an identical net-profit contribution.

metrics.label: Calculated sum; fiscal year ended September 28, 2025

slides.svgBlueprint: Build three full-width receipt rows with monospaced numerical badges and separate million labels. Use a small plus sign between the first two rows and a double accounting rule above the total. Highlight only the total row in red. Place REVENUE in a rectangular outline stamp; do not use a profit label or a percentage chart.

slides.headline: Automatic Reload Keeps Customer Financing Flowing
slides.subheadline: Date or balance triggers replenish interest-free prepayments; Starbucks seeks more visits.​

items.title: CANCELLATION WINDOW
items.body: Cancel at least twenty-four (24) hours before the next scheduled reload.

items.title: SETTINGS ARE NOT REVERSALS
items.body: Preference changes can lag; completed loads cannot be reversed under the automatic-reload provision.

slides.svgBlueprint: Create two tall control panels beneath the headline. Use a simple clock arc in the cancellation panel and a reload arrow ending at a solid stop bar in the settings panel. Show both 24 badges at 52px, placing at least and up to on separate lines. Keep arrows inside panels and avoid suggesting automatic reload is mandatory.

slides.headline: Prepayment Is Financing. Revenue Is Not Profit.
slides.subheadline: Keep convenience, reject the savings-account analogy, and use applicable cash-out rights.​

items.title: THE FINANCIAL RECORD
items.body: Customers provide interest-free financing; recognized nonredemption revenue does not establish equivalent net profit.​

items.title: CALIFORNIA CASH-OUT
items.body: Request cash for qualifying balances strictly below $15, including electronic gift cards.

items.title: REWARDS WITHOUT PRELOADING
items.body: Fiscal 2025: members could earn Stars using cash, credit, debit or selected wallets at participating locations.

metrics.label: California qualifying cash-out threshold—not $15 or less

slides.svgBlueprint: Give the middle cash-out item a full-width hero placard. Set strictly below above an 84px $15 badge, with the effective-date badge beneath it. Place the financial verdict in a compact surface card above and the rewards alternative in one below. Finish with a red rule and The Fine Print masthead; avoid bank imagery or claims that every balance qualifies.
